title: Jelly Roll Martin and the London Blues recording with Buster Bailey and Zutty Robinson
summary: Dominique recorded London Blues and Sunday Sweetheart with Jelly Roll Martin, Buster Bailey, a nervous Zoo Robinson and others.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: What was the style like on piano? Almost like Jellarole Martin.
I like Jellarole Martin. And I work with Jellarole Martin too. That's why I work with Jellarole Martin.
I know your first record just made it.
Jellarole Martin. London Blues, I think it was.
Sunday Sweetheart. That's the time Buster Bailey, Zoo Robinson. We had Johnny Sincere guitar. Who was playing bass? I think Bill Johnson was playing bass. I'm not mistaken. The Jellarole Martin.
Could it have been the Horace Eubanks song?

No, I could have had a record though with Horace Eubanks. That London Blues, the Sunday Sweetheart, that was with Buster Bailey. Buster Bailey. Buster Bailey, that's in New York now. That played with John Kirby's band.
Zoo on trombone. Man, that was a nervous guy too. He was so nervous.
Pull up and show his socks.
Yeah, show his socks, show everything.

Good musician. Come on out, come on out. They played some good bass since then. They played good bass. And give them a solo to play a nice solo. Beautiful. But I don't know who taught Zoo Robinson. And I have it in me.
Somebody's name is Alil, maybe I'm not sure. But I don't know who taught him.
I'm not going to tell you no story. No. No, it's not me telling a story. I'm trying to tell you everything and the facts about it.
